newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols firm as spot edges lower.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols firm as spot edges lower.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options continued to firm in U.S. trading Tuesday after the spot's break below 114 yen the previous day reignited interest in downside strikes, options dealers and analysts said.
The renewed activity helped push dollar/yen risk reversals, the put-call pricing differential, back over the 2.0 threshold favoring yen calls on one-month options, dealers said.
Last week, one-month 25-delta risk reversals were slanted as high as 2.5 percent for yen calls when the dollar fell just shy of 110.
This morning, an options dealer said a one-month 20-delta risk reversal traded at 2.6. One-month 25-delta risk reversals were quoted at 2.0/2.4.
Dollar/yen was bid at 113.38 around midday, after briefly dipping below 113.00.
"I don't think most participants believe the 113.00-113.50 area is where the dollar is going to sit," said Alan Revercomb, options strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.
Dealers said low-delta short-dated dollar/yen options in 108 through 110 strikes have been popular this morning.

Good demand for yen calls and dollar puts continues to flow from corporate end-users looking to hedge long dollar exposure and from dealers seeking to cover their short gamma positions, preserving the strong yen call bias on risk reversals and bolstering volatilities, Revercomb said.
"Now," he said, "we're getting a new round of speculative interest on the downside."
In this spot-sensitive market, Revercomb said, a slide below 112.00 would heighten nervousness, while it would take a challenge of trendline resistance at 115.70 to shift the focus to the upside.
"Any initial move higher will continue to be met with lower vols," he said.
One-month dollar/yen volatility was 13.1/13.4 percent, up from 12.6/12.9 percent Monday. One-year rose commensurately to 11.1/11.3 percent.

Also supporting volatilities are upcoming Japanese and U.S. trade data, which arrive just before this weekend's G7 summit in Denver. May Japanese trade balance figures are due out at 2350 GMT, and U.S. April trade data are scheduled for Thursday. Both are expected to show a widening of Japan's surplus with the U.S.
Dollar/mark volatilities were slightly lower, at 9.2/9.5 percent for one-month options and 9.3/9.6 percent for one-years.
While there has been a lot of talk of value in dollar/mark vols, "the reality is dollar/mark hasn't been volatile," Revercomb said.
